'''Harry Friedmann''' ({{langx|he|הארי פרידמן}}; 28 November 1931 – 28 May 2018) was a professor of chemistry who specialized in theoretical [[nonlinear optics]] and [[List of laser applications|lasers in biology]].

==Biography==
Harry Friedmann<ref name="chem">{{Cite web |title=Friedmann Harry {{!}} Department of Chemistry    {{!}} Bar-Ilan University |url=https://ch.biu.ac.il/node/1643 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181113210549/https://ch.biu.ac.il/node/1643 |archive-date=2018-11-13 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=ch.biu.ac.il |language=en }}</ref> (1931–2018) was born in [[Frankfurt|Frankfurt am Main]] to Miriam (Manya) and Moshe Friedmann. Soon after his birth, the family fled to [[Czechoslovakia]] to the area that was called the [[Sudetenland]] and from there to [[Belgium]]. He studied at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] from 1951, gaining a Ph.D. with distinction in 1964 under the supervision of [[List of Nobel laureates|Nobel prize winner]] [[Ilya Prigogine]]. He was a research associate at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] (1962–1967), a senior lecturer at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] (1967–1969) and then a professor at [[Bar-Ilan University]] in the Chemistry Department.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Chemistry {{!}} Bar-Ilan University |url=https://ch.biu.ac.il/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=ch.biu.ac.il}}</ref> He became a professor emeritus at Bar-Ilan University in 1999.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Prof. Harry Friedmann |url=https://research.biu.ac.il/researcher/professor-harry-friedmann/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190422154235/https://research.biu.ac.il/researcher/professor-harry-friedmann/ |archive-date=2019-04-22 |access-date=2025-05-21 |work=The Bar-Ilan University (BIU) Research Authority |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref> Friedmann was married to Josephine and had two children, Jacqueline Perle and Daniel, and five grandchildren.

==Scientific interests and publications==
His research<ref name=chem></ref><ref>[https://biu.academia.edu/HarryFriedmann Harry Friedmann - Academia.edu]</ref> focused on [[quantum statistical mechanics]],<ref name="Friedmann2007">{{cite book|last1=Friedmann|first1=H.|title=Advances in Chemical Physics |chapter=The Quantum Mechanical Distribution Function of Molecular Systems: Translational and Rotational Motions|year=1962|pages=225–302|issn=1934-4791|doi=10.1002/9780470143506.ch6|isbn=978-0-470-14350-6 }}</ref> [[spectroscopy#Molecules|spectroscopy of molecules]] in [[Noble gas|rare-gas]] [[crystals]],<ref name="FriedmannKimel1967">{{cite journal|last1=Friedmann|first1=H.|last2=Kimel|first2=S.|author-link2=Sol Kimel|title=Rotation—Translation‐Coupling Effect in Noble‐Gas Crystals Containing Molecular Impurities|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=47|issue=9|year=1967|pages=3589–3605|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.1712427|bibcode=1967JChPh..47.3589F }}</ref> theoretical [[nonlinear optics]], especially [[isotope separation]],<ref name="FriedmannWilson1976">{{cite journal|last1=Friedmann|first1=H.|last2=Wilson|first2=A. D.|title=Isotope separation by radiation pressure of coherent π pulses|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=28|issue=5|year=1976|pages=270–272|issn=0003-6951|doi=10.1063/1.88731|bibcode=1976ApPhL..28..270F }}</ref><ref name="FriedmannAhiman1980">{{cite journal|last1=Friedmann|first1=H.|last2=Ahiman|first2=V.|title=Transition from bloch equations to rate equations for multiple photon excitation of polyatomic molecules|journal=Optics Communications|volume=33|issue=2|year=1980|pages=163–168|issn=0030-4018|doi=10.1016/0030-4018(80)90185-6|bibcode=1980OptCo..33..163F }}</ref> [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear]] optical processes in [[Atomic physics|atomic systems]],<ref name="FriedmannWilson-Gordon1982">{{cite journal|last1=Friedmann|first1=H.|last2=Wilson-Gordon|first2=A. D.|title=Extra resonances in four-wave mixing triggered by radiative relaxation|journal=Physical Review A|volume=26|issue=5|year=1982|pages=2768–2777|issn=0556-2791|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.26.2768|bibcode=1982PhRvA..26.2768F }}</ref><ref name="Wilson-GordonFriedmann1989">{{cite journal|last1=Wilson-Gordon|first1=A. D.|last2=Friedmann|first2=H.|title=Ultranarrow extraresonant antiholes in pump–probe spectroscopy induced by inelastic collisions|journal=Optics Letters|volume=14|issue=8|year=1989|page=390|issn=0146-9592|doi=10.1364/OL.14.000390|pmid=19749930 |bibcode=1989OptL...14..390W }}</ref><ref name="Wilson-GordonFriedmann1992">{{cite journal|last1=Wilson-Gordon|first1=A.D.|last2=Friedmann|first2=H.|title=Enhanced index of refraction: a comparison between two- and three-level systems|journal=Optics Communications|volume=94|issue=4|year=1992|pages=238–244|issn=0030-4018|doi=10.1016/0030-4018(92)90020-R|bibcode=1992OptCo..94..238W }}</ref><ref name="GorenWilson-Gordon2003">{{cite journal|last1=Goren|first1=C.|last2=Wilson-Gordon|first2=A. D.|last3=Rosenbluh|first3=M.|last4=Friedmann|first4=H.|title=Electromagnetically induced absorption due to transfer of coherence and to transfer of population|journal=Physical Review A|volume=67|issue=3|year=2003|article-number=033807 |issn=1050-2947|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.67.033807|bibcode=2003PhRvA..67c3807G }}</ref> [[Electromagnetic radiation|light propagation]] and [[Optical storage|storage]],<ref name="Bortman-ArbivWilson-Gordon2001">{{cite journal|last1=Bortman-Arbiv|first1=D.|last2=Wilson-Gordon|first2=A. D.|last3=Friedmann|first3=H.|title=Phase control of group velocity: From subluminal to superluminal light propagation|journal=Physical Review A|volume=63|issue=4|year=2001|article-number=043818 |issn=1050-2947|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.63.043818|bibcode=2001PhRvA..63d3818B }}</ref><ref name="ShpaismanWilson-Gordon2005">{{cite journal|last1=Shpaisman|first1=H.|last2=Wilson-Gordon|first2=A. He published over 120 papers in peer-reviewed journals, many of them co-authored by colleagues [[Arlene Wilson-Gordon]] and Rachel Lubart.<ref name=chem></ref>
